clue.text: Those people with old British criminal gang

parts.note: them refers to those people

explanation.surface: Someone points out a group of people who once belonged to a notorious British gang.
explanation.definitionFit: The mob is the collective term for organised crime, a syndicate of gangsters.

clue.text: Managed to interrupt Tory leader William's angry speech

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so this piece goes inside the name

parts.note: William Hague led the Conservative (Tory) Party from 1997 to 2001
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone managed to cut in on a ranting speech by William Hague.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague was leader of the UK Conservative Party, nicknamed the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a lengthy, aggressive or ranting address.

clue.text: State I'm aching after treatment

indicators.note: after treatment means once worked on and altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient declares they ache after medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning declare, but it is the noun for a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Michigan is one of the fifty United States, in the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Save money for pub worker

parts.note: save in the sense of except is bar, as in all bar one
tender is money, as in legal tender

explanation.surface: Advice to put cash aside to pay a barman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a verb about keeping money, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks behind the counter in a bar or pub.

clue.text: University representative I call is officiating

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A student union spokesperson says they are calling a match as referee.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire officiates at cricket or tennis, so umpiring is acting as the match official.

clue.text: Not playing by the rules? In part, Elon Musk's reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Says Elon Musk is partly reformed after breaking the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' looks like a hidden-word signal, but the words are all anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsportsmanlike conduct is unfair play, breaking the spirit or rules of a game.

clue.text: Press love dealing with valuable material

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
re means regarding or concerning

explanation.surface: Instructions to press something precious with tender care.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron ore is rock mined for its metal content, a valuable raw resource.

clue.text: Unclothed, wear thin pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a poor arrangement to be reordered

explanation.surface: Someone naked wears skimpy underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pants' as an adjective means bad, which hides the anagram signal inside underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: In the raw is an idiom for naked, with nothing on.

clue.text: Betting American wears good jewellery

indicators.note: wears means has on, so the outer pieces enclose this one

parts.note: bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A US citizen is decked out in fine jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' reads as the American wearing jewellery, but the good jewellery wears the American: the abbreviation sits between the two outer pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling is wagering money on the outcome of a game or event.

clue.text: Gets hold of expert remedies

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
cures are remedies

explanation.surface: Someone obtains treatments recommended by a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure is to obtain or acquire something, often with some effort.

clue.text: Shakespeare character who was a bit of an ass saying bravo when returning

definitions.text: Shakespeare character who was a bit of an ass

indicators.note: returning means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a motto is a saying
Bravo is B in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A description of a comic Shakespeare character shouting bravo on his way back.
explanation.walkthrough: MOTTO followed by B gives MOTTOB, which read backwards is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Bottom, the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, is given a donkey's head by Puck, so he was partly an ass.

clue.text: Another novel about one flawed protagonist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the piece for one
novel means new or fresh, so the letters of another are made anew in a different order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A reader describes yet another book centred on a flawed hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' turns ANOTHER into ANTHERO, and 'about' puts I inside it, after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character lacking conventional heroic virtues, a deeply imperfect lead.

clue.text: Succeed in party we're going to

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
we'll is the contraction of we will, meaning we're going to; the apostrophe is ignored

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to have a good time at a party they and friends are attending.
explanation.definitionFit: To do well is to prosper or achieve success.

clue.text: Charlie leaves very moreish E number, say

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so this letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: something very moreish makes you want more, so is addictive
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie abandons a tasty treat that has a food additive in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moreish' is a British word for food so tasty you want more of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An E number is a code for an approved food additive such as a colouring or preservative; 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Struggle with core argument's perspective

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
the point is the central argument

explanation.surface: Someone wrestling with the crux of a debate's angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewpoint is an opinion or way of seeing things.

clue.text: Passionate, outspoken ex-footballer Roy

indicators.note: outspoken means spoken aloud, so the name is replaced by a word sounding the same

parts.note: Roy Keane is a former Manchester United and Ireland captain

explanation.surface: Describes Roy Keane, the fiery Irish former footballer known for his blunt opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Keane, now a television pundit, is famous for being outspoken, which hides the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen means eager or enthusiastic, so it matches passionate.

clue.text: Collapse from Kane disheartened English fan

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, the middle, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters of Kane
a lover of something is a fan of it

explanation.surface: An England fan collapses, dejected by Harry Kane's performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Kane is England's football captain.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to fall down suddenly, as a capsized boat does.

clue.text: Cheap yet fancy pirate's accessory?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: A costume item for a pirate that is cheap yet stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates are traditionally pictured wearing a cloth cover over one lost eye.

clue.text: Wings of sparrow injuring large swallow

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two ends, so take the first and last letters of each word

parts.note: first and last letters of sparrow
first and last letters of injuring

explanation.surface: A sparrow's wings are being hurt by a large swallow, one bird attacking another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like the bird beside the sparrow, but it is the verb for drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a big gulp of drink, a large mouthful taken at once.

clue.text: The Police's leader admitting everyone is playing for time

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: Sting was the frontman of the rock band The Police
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A police chief lets everyone in while delaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Police' is the rock band, not the force; its leader is Sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalling is delaying deliberately to gain time.

clue.text: One brings in products, shrimp or terrine sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the answer is held inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A food trader's sandwiches are filled with shrimp or terrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food, fitting shrimp and terrine, but it is the verb for enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer buys goods from abroad and ships them into the country.

clue.text: Tattoo mad brute designed

indicators.note: designed means arranged or planned out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazy thug has drawn up a tattoo pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tattoo' suggests body art, but here it means a rhythmic beating of a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is also a rhythmic drum signal or a military display, so a drumbeat.

clue.text: Couple upset an editor showing some guts

parts.note: a duo is a couple, a pair

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so these letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A couple are distressed by an editor showing courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' looks like bravery, but it is the literal intestines.
explanation.definitionFit: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine; duodena is the plural.

clue.text: Small PC left with suitable work

parts.note: apt means suitable
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A little computer was abandoned alongside a fitting job.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer, a compact one.

clue.text: French refusal to accept a European emperor

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the refusal holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: non is French for no
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A French no to welcoming a European emperor into the fold.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: Serve to Edberg partially blocked

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tennis serve to Stefan Edberg was partly blocked by the receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: Stefan Edberg is a Swedish former tennis champion, which makes 'Serve' look like a tennis term.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto is to forbid or stop a proposal, so vetoed means it was prevented.

clue.text: Launch trendy, current art gallery, visited by yours truly

parts.note: in means fashionable
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: visited by means someone goes into the gallery, so one letter goes inside it

parts.note: the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain
yours truly is a jokey way of saying I, me

explanation.surface: An announcement that the speaker visited to open a fashionable contemporary art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to begin or set something going, just as one starts a venture.

clue.text: Run through outskirts of Rochdale with black car

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so take the first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of Rochdale
a hearse is a usually black vehicle carrying a coffin

explanation.surface: A funeral car drives around the edge of Rochdale, a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a performance, going through it in preparation.

clue.text: Rows about leader of Guides or Cubs?

indicators.note: about means around, so the rows go round the letter

parts.note: tiers are rows, as of seats

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Guides

explanation.surface: Disputes over who heads the Girl Guides or Cub Scouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels but means layers; 'Cubs' looks like young Scouts but means the young of big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Young tigers are called cubs, so cubs may be tigers; the question mark signals the example.
